llm.summary: The yield-relief trade that let the Nasdaq print a record yesterday has fully reversed: the 10-year is above 5.3% and the 30-year is back at its highest since 2002 ahead of a key auction, Brent is back above $100 on Houthi/Hormuz risk, and the dollar is firm. Gold broke below $4,100 and silver fell, confirming again that real yields and the dollar — not Fed pricing — are the binding constraint on hard assets. The real-economy transmission is now visible and fast: 30-year mortgages at 7.49% (near a three-year high), refi demand at half of last year, lock volumes plunging, and heating oil bills forecast up 21% this winter. Meanwhile the AI capex machine escalated again — SpaceX is seeking $40bn of debt (Apollo expected to lead) purely to buy Nvidia chips, Nvidia is reportedly planning $1bn into Figure, and the $20bn Groq transaction is drawing a lawsuit; this is no longer cash-flow-funded capex but a credit structure. Google's 3.6 GW deal with Constellation Energy extends yesterday's nuclear PPA into the single most contracted earnings stream in the market, against Utilities flows at -84 and Real Estate at -92. The regime model keeps drifting away from both clean outcomes: Contraction -5.4 and Goldilocks -3.6, while Reflation +4.8 and Stagflation +4.1 — higher nominal growth with sticky prices, which is exactly what $100 oil plus a 5.3% long end encodes. Flows remain a one-sector market: Technology +85, everything else negative, growth over value by 103 points, the widest in the series. For the book, DXCM gapping -4% pre-market with Health Care flows at -48 is the live problem; SMCI/HPQ remain levered to memory pricing and to a long end that is moving the wrong way.

market_thesis.short_term: Days-to-weeks: this is a vice, not a trend. Earnings and AI order flow are genuinely accelerating (AMD server commentary, Broadcom, 20,000 Rubin GPUs ordered in India, Aehr follow-on orders for a hyperscale AI processor) while the discount rate rises and energy re-inflates. Fed minutes today land against a tape that has already re-priced toward Reflation/Stagflation; a hawkish read plus a sloppy long-bond auction takes the 30-year through its 2002 high decisively and the index gives back the record. Positioning is dangerously narrow — Technology at +85 against ten negative sectors means there is no second leg to catch a Tech wobble. Own things paid in contracted dollars (power PPAs, security subscriptions reaffirmed by Zscaler, defense backlog) and avoid anything whose thesis requires the long end to fall. Expect gold to stay capped while the dollar firms, and expect every rate-sensitive consumer datapoint (housing, autos, heating bills) to keep deteriorating regardless of what the S&P does.
market_thesis.medium_term: Months: the defining shift is that AI capex has migrated to external leverage. SpaceX borrowing roughly a year of revenue to buy GPUs, Apollo leading, record bank-arranged chip financings, Anthropic prepping an IPO — the build continues but it becomes a credit story with residual-value risk on depreciating silicon. That favours the toll-takers on utilisation over the levered buyers: silicon and networking (NVDA, AVGO, MRVL, MU), the semicap layer (AMAT, LRCX, ASML), and above all electrons. Power is the least-contested earnings stream on the tape — Google/Constellation 3.6 GW, Meta's seven gas plants, Southeast Asia at 5.4% demand growth, El Niño raising load — while Utilities flows sit at -84 and CEG/VST/EQT show high attention with low pricing. That gap closes. Macro stays reflationary-with-sticky-prices: $100 oil, a widest-since-pre-tariff trade deficit, RBI hiking, term premium elevated by fiscal supply. Housing stays impaired at 7.49% and the consumer keeps splitting — off-price and value retail take share while discretionary categories (beer, big-ticket, new autos) soften.
market_thesis.long_term: Years: three structural lines. First, compute and generation are one capital decision; an advertising company funding gas plants and a search company signing multi-gigawatt nuclear capacity says the scarce input is firm power, not models. Owning generation, the fuel cycle, grid equipment and cooling is the most durable claim on AI, and it will be revalued upward from flow-depressed levels. Second, agents become the interface and the metering layer: ChatGPT retaining consumer lead with spend concentrated in power users (top 1% > bottom 50%), Meta's Muse topping charts, Microsoft/Nvidia putting agents into Windows laptops, and Meta/Walmart/Stripe/Shopify backing an agent interoperability standard. Whoever owns identity, delegation, payment rails and runtime containment for agents collects a per-action toll — which is why Cybersecurity sits atop the flow ranking. Third, the cost of capital has structurally reset: a 5.3% long end with debt service above nominal growth means permanent term premium, chronic housing undersupply because nothing pencils at 7.5%, and a decade where, as BofA warns, equity returns may not clear bonds. Capital-light productivity and hard physical assets with contracted cash flows win; levered duration and asset gatherers lose.

short_term: Households are being squeezed on non-discretionary energy: heating oil bills projected up 21% this winter, which transfers wallet share away from discretionary goods and services in Q4-Q1.

Housing transactions are freezing rather than repricing — refi demand is half of last year, mortgage lock volumes plunged in September, and at 7.49% move-up buyers simply stay put. Demand shifts to repair/remodel and rental.
Car buyers are trading down and optimising for running cost: used prices fell in Q3 while demand for fuel-efficient vehicles grew.

Consumer AI spend is concentrating, not broadening — the top 1% of AI spenders exceed the bottom 50% combined; the mass-market monetisation moment has not arrived and Meta's Muse must convert novelty into habit.
Discretionary consumption is bifurcating visibly: Constellation Brands flagging durability questions in beer demand and cutting the market's FY27 expectations, while off-price (TJX) holds up.
Investors are abandoning long-duration assets — long Treasury flows decreasing, gold ETFs bleeding on higher real yields, small-caps negative — and crowding into one sector.
Young voters have decoupled housing aspiration from political expectation, which is an early marker of durable deferral of household formation.
long_term: Energy security moves from a policy abstraction to a household budget line and a corporate siting decision; people will pay for reliability (backup, efficiency, insulation, heat pumps) the way they pay for insurance.

Delegation replaces search: people will increasingly want outcomes executed by agents rather than information retrieved, which rewires advertising, payments, and the trust/identity layer that must authorise bots.
Stablecoins graduate from speculation to plumbing — the sharp rise in mainstream stablecoin queries signals demand for cheap, instant, dollar-denominated settlement, especially cross-border.

Permanently higher mortgage rates convert housing from an ownership ladder into a rental/multigenerational service, raising demand for build-to-rent, manufactured housing, and renovation over new transactions.

Security of the physical kind becomes consumer-salient: drone-warfare attention spiking, attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure, and Hormuz risk normalise defense as an investable civic need rather than a cyclical trade.

Healthspan spending becomes self-directed and continuous (monitoring, metabolic, aesthetics) even as institutional health-care capital flows deteriorate — a divergence between patient demand and sector flows.
